This method surpasses the Single-Time-Over-Threshold (STOT) by precisely determining both the number of vacuum ultraviolet (VUV) photons detected by each photomultiplier tube (PMT) and their arrival times for light signal measurement.

title: De-novo whole genome assembly of the orange jewelweed, Impatiens capensis Meerb. (Balsaminaceae) using nanopore long-read sequencing
creator: Sudhindra R. Gadagkar, J. Antonio Baeza, Kristina Buss, Nate Johnson
description: The plant family Balsaminaceae comprises only two genera, and they are a study in contrasts. While Impatiens is an impressively prolific genus, with over 1,000 species and more being discovered each year, its sister genus, Hydrocera, has one solitary species, H. triflora.

title: Trends in suicidal thoughts, suicide attempts and self-harm in England
creator: S McManus
description: BackgroundMany countries have experienced increases in the number of people attending health care services after self-harm. The prevalence of self-harm in the community, which includes people who do not contact health services, is greater. This means population-based surveys are essential to understanding the prevalence and distribution of self-harm.

title: Anti-Inflammatory Effect of Dietary Pentadecanoic Fatty Acid Supplementation on Inflammatory Bowel Disease in SAMP1/YitFc Mice
creator: Drishtant Singh, Paola Mehghini, Alexander Rodriguez-Palacios, Luca Di Martino, Fabio Cominelli, Abigail Raffner Basson
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background/Objectives: Dietary fats have been linked to the increasing incidence of chronic diseases, including inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD), namely, Crohn’s disease (CD). Methods: This study investigated the impact of pentadecanoic acid (C15:0), a type of an odd-numbered chain saturated fatty acid, for its potential anti-inflammatory properties in different mouse models of experimental IBD using the SAMP1/YitFc (SAMP) mouse line (14- or 24-week-old), including chronic ileitis and DSS-induced colitis.

title: Effects of a peer coaching intervention for occupational physicians on time allocated to prevention
creator: S Orhan Pees, SH van Oostrom, FG Schaafsma, KI Proper
description: BackgroundWhile the importance of prevention in the workplace is widely recognized, the implementation of preventive tasks by occupational physicians (OPs) in the Netherlands remains limited. To support OPs in their preventive role, a peer coaching intervention was developed and implemented in existing peer groups.

title: Determination of Dipicolinic Acid through the Antenna Effect of Eu(III) Coordination Polymer
creator: Jing Li, Yu Liang, Chun Tian, Hongyan Zou, Lei Zhan, Lijuan Wang, Chengzhi Huang, Chunmei Li, Michal Szostak, Graham Saunders
description: Bacillus anthracis is a Gram-positive bacterium that can cause acute infection and anthracnose, which is a serious concern for human health. Determining Bacillus anthracis through its spore biomarker dipicolinic acid (DPA) is crucial, and there is a strong need for a method that is rapid, sensitive, and selective.

title: The Concentration of Follistatin and Activin A in Serum and Selected Biochemical Parameters in Women with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: Stratification by Tobacco Smoke Exposure, Insulin Resistance, and Overweight/Obesity
creator: Justyna Niepsuj, Agnieszka Piwowar, Grzegorz Franik, Anna Bizoń, Alberto Revelli
description: Background/Objectives: The aim of the study was to investigate the concentrations of follistatin and activin A in the serum of women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and to assess their relationship with selected biochemical parameters, specifically stratifying the analysis based on tobacco smoke, insulin resistance, and abnormal weight.

title: Androgen Deprivation Therapy and the Risk of Newly Developed Dry Eye Syndrome in Patients with Prostate Cancer: A Nationwide Nested Case–Control Study in the Republic of Korea
creator: Jinhyung Jeon, Jee Soo Ha, Hye Sun Lee, Soyoung Jeon, Ho Sik Hwang, Daeho Kim, June Seok Kim, Byeong Seon Kim, Min Kim, Kang Su Cho
description: Background: We aimed to evaluate the association between androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) and newly developed dry eye syndrome (DES) in patients with prostate cancer. Methods: A nested case–control study was conducted. From the nationwide claims database of the Republic of Korea, 125,005 patients were included in the final analysis.

title: The Biosynthesis of Bacterial Cellulose Composites Accompanied by Spray Feeding of Biomasses
creator: Jiali Xu, Xiaodi Liu, Qiang Zhang, Luis Alves
description: Bacterial cellulose (BC) is a broadly utilized natural nanofiber produced by microbial fermentation, but its high-cost and low-yield production and limited function still hinder its application. Here, we used the spraying-assisted biosynthesis method to introduce biomass nanofibers along with the nutrient media to the fermenting BC. Biomass nanofibers could be cellulose, chitosan, and others.

title: The association between health literacy and multiple health risk behaviors
creator: EV Kang, SE Kim, JG Cho, YJ Won
description: BackgroundClustered modifiable behaviors-smoking, high-risk alcohol use, physical inactivity, and high sodium intake-drive a sizable share of the premature non-communicable disease burden. Managing these co-occurring risks may depend on health literacy (HL), the ability to find, understand, and use health information. This study examined the association between HL and multiple health risk behaviors (MHRBs) using nationally representative data from South Korea.

title: Community centred mental health provision for young people
creator: S Sykes, J Wills, G Bridge, J Oha, P Reavey, P Callaghan
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundTraditional mental health services for young people often require clinical diagnoses, operate rigid age thresholds, and rely on complex referral pathways - contributing to unmet need and disengagement. This evaluation adds to a growing evidence base on place-based mental health, examining a community programme with 4 projects including: 8 weeks of one-to-one support via Wellbeing Navigators, arts-based Community Hubs providing creative, inclusive spaces for support, a whole school approach to promoting mental health, and staff training.MethodsA co-produced theory of change was developed.

title: Motorcyclist visibility materials uptake and associated factors toward injury prevention in Cameroon
creator: C E Ukah, N Tendongfor, A Hubbard, E A Tanue, N Bassah, R Oke, S A Christie, L K Yunika, C Julliard, A Chichom-Mefire
description: BackgroundCommercial motorcycle riders in Cameroon are highly vulnerable road users, often exposed to traffic injuries and fatalities. Low visibility, especially in poor lighting, is a key contributor to crashes. Although visibility materials such as reflective jackets, stickers, and lights help prevent injuries, awareness and consistent use remain limited in many low- and middle-income settings.

title: Building Trust Through Transparency: Reimagining Communication in the Secondary Use of Health Data
creator: R M Hansen, L G Jensen, D Kalra, M D Terkildsen
description: BackgroundAs AI-driven health data platforms like IDERHA scale across Europe, secondary use of personal health data raises ethical and public health challenges around trust and transparency. Conventional models of transparency, rooted in compliance or disclosure, often fall short in building sustained trust among diverse populations.

title: The use of age-period-cohort models in the Dutch public health foresight study
creator: M Buijs, G De Boer, MHD Plasmans, H Hilderink
description: BackgroundThe Dutch Public Health Foresight Study 2024 (PHFS) provides an outlook on future trends in public health and care. However, projecting incidence, prevalence, and mortality is challenging due to uncertainties in contextual factors like societal, economic, and technological developments. It is therefore crucial to utilize all available data from recent cohorts.

title: Sports coaches’ perception of Health Promotion: philosophies, actions, barriers & strategies study
creator: K Barros, A Lefebvre, A Van Hoye
description: BackgroundSport coaches play an essential role in promoting the health of sport participants, yet their contribution is often underemphasized, despite sports clubs being recognized as health-promoting settings. This article explores sports coaches’ philosophies, actions, barriers and strategies to health promotion (HP).MethodsAn exploratory mixed-method survey design (QUAL = >quan) was used in this study.

title: Digital and Social Inclusion as Determinants of Emotional Well-Being in Older Europeans
creator: J Lera, M Barreda, D Cantarero-Prieto
description: BackgroundAs populations age across Europe, ensuring emotional well-being in later life has become a pressing public health priority. While social isolation and depressive symptoms are prevalent in older adults, digital engagement and social integration may act as protective factors. This study examines how internet use and social connectedness relate to emotional well-being-measured through loneliness and depressive symptoms-among Europeans aged 50+.

title: Environmental impact of diet from the INRAN-SCAI Survey: role of food groups and health determinants
creator: D Lacalaprice, N Scarsi, F Gianfagna, A Paladini, S Boccia, R Pastorino
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe environmental impacts of food consumption, specifically carbon footprint (CF) and water footprint (WF), are gaining increasing importance in the context of global sustainability and public health. This study evaluates the contribution of different food groups to environmental footprints and examines how health determinants such as gender, age, BMI, geographic location, and adherence to the Mediterranean diet (MD) influence these impacts.

title: Empowering Socially Vulnerable Older Adults: The AHAA Project's Holistic Health Literacy Approach
creator: J Vanderlinden, S Lambers, S Van Rampelberg, P J Verschelden
description: BackgroundThe ‘Active and Healthy Ageing for All’ (AHAA) project, initiated by Odisee University of Applied Sciences in Belgium, aims to enhance the health literacy of home-dwelling older adults. This project addresses the need for tailored health education programs for socially disadvantaged older adults, who are often underserved by conventional preventive health initiatives.

title: Associations between diabetes and depressive symptoms across European countries
creator: J Gottfried, G Flynn, K Gajewska, R A Kenny, B Hernández, C Lloyd, A Nouwen, S Power, R Rodrigues, S Deschênes
description: BackgroundWe examined the potential role of several macro- and micro-sociodemographic factors in moderating the longitudinal bi-directional association between depressive symptom severity and diabetes across European countries. This submission summarizes the results of two empirical studies and workshop-based group discussions with people living with diabetes.

title: Accuracy of PoCT devices for glycated hemoglobin in outpatient settings: a scoping review
creator: E Duim, R Q de Araujo, B S Breternitz, A B Andrade, E T Rother, P C de Freitas, LAA Menezes Junior, OGE Martinez, L O Cardoso, MLP Ferrer
description: BackgroundEarly screening for type 2 diabetes mellitus is a global public health priority. Point-of-care testing (PoCT) technologies offer a promising alternative to diagnosis and monitoring of metabolic risk. However, it is essential to assess the accuracy of these devices compared to golden standart methods.ObjectivesTo map the diagnostic accuracy of PoCT devices for HbA1c used in outpatient settings.

title: Scaling up a psychological intervention for alcohol misuse in wartime: a qualitative study in Ukraine
creator: K Antia, C Van Der Boor, O Biklian, V Kachay, S Bogdanov, B Roberts, D Fuhr
description: BackgroundThe war in Ukraine has intensified mental health vulnerabilities, including alcohol misuse among conflict-affected men. The CHANGE intervention, a new transdiagnostic intervention building on WHO's Problem Management Plus (PM+), aims to address alcohol misuse and common mental disorders. This study explores the scalability of CHANGE within Ukraine's war-affected health system.

title: A community-based intervention to reduce loneliness in young adults: components and implementation
creator: C Duarte, A Niaz, J Lau
description: BackgroundLoneliness is recognised as an urgent public health concern, associated with adverse mental and physical health outcomes. While most interventions are aimed at older adults, young and working-age adults have been identified as being at risk for persistent loneliness. Despite this, there remains limited understanding of the evidence base for interventions targeting this age group.

title: Addressing youth loneliness: Development and validation of the youth loneliness scale
creator: L Riddleston, L Verity, D Fuhrmann, I Alam, J Conway, P Spowage, L Turner, W Walibhai, P Qualter, JYF Lau
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundLoneliness has emerged as a significant public health issue, recognized as a priority by the UK government. Particularly prevalent among young people, approximately 50% of individuals aged 10-24 report experiencing loneliness “often” or “some of the time.” This persistent sense of isolation is associated with a range of negative outcomes, including poor mental and physical health, lower educational achievement, and diminished employment prospects.

title: Beyond personal responsibility: the protective role of work-life balance crafting in remote work
creator: V Krūmiņa, K Mārtinsone, E Akmane, A Ķule, D Kamerāde, L Matisāne, L Paegle, M Matisāne, S Lakisa, I Vanadziņš
description: Sociological survey in Latvia (Kantar, 2024) found that 39% of individuals consider work-life balance (WLB) a personal responsibility. While WLB is often addressed through research of specific strategies’ impact, our study explored whether individual-level behaviours - referred to as WLB crafting (WLBC) - are associated with a greater sense of balance among remote workers.

title: Health Spending and NCD Mortality in the Western Balkans: Trends, Outcomes, and Policy Lessons
creator: J Gabrani, A Anton, S Cilović-Lagarija, D Grujic, M Petrovski, N Rosic, N Terzic, M M Šantrić-Milićević, A Romel, S Skočibušić
description: BackgroundNon-communicable diseases (NCDs) remain the primary causes of mortality worldwide. In the Western Balkans, cardiovascular diseases, cancers, and chronic respiratory diseases account for a substantial proportion of deaths, placing considerable strain on health systems and economies. While health expenditures increased between 2013 and 2021, the extent to which this translated into improved NCD outcomes remains uncertain.

title: Anxiety and depression as predictors of NEET in young adulthood: A Swedish national cohort study
creator: J Wahlström, V Östberg, S B Låftman
description: BackgroundYoung people not in education, employment, or training (NEET) are a growing concern in European societies. While mental health problems are established risk factors for NEET status, the specific roles of anxiety and depression - and their co-occurrence - remains understudied.

title: Constructing the Estimates: Computational Methods in Burden of Foodborne Diseases
creator: L Vaes, C Di Bari, K Fernandez, B Devleesschauwer
description: In the first iteration of the global burden of foodborne diseases, various approaches for imputing missing incidence data at country level were tested and evaluated. In this iteration estimates were presented at subregional level without a time trend. For the second iteration we aimed to have country and year estimates.

title: Implementation of community health interventions for adolescents in LMICs: a scoping review
creator: P Absetz, M Oyanga, H Koros, L Mlunde, M Seynou, E Gobbo, A Ojwang
description: BackgroundAdolescents in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) face multiple health challenges, including rising burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) and limited access to health services. Community-based interventions could promote adolescent health, but their sustainability is a challenge. This scoping review aimed to identify implementation strategies, barriers, and facilitators for sustainability.

title: BeWell: Shaping the future health workforce with innovative digital and green skills training
creator: F Margheri, L Ninov, L Mathey
description: EU countries have increasingly focused on embracing digital and green solutions in health. The BeWell project offers a training framework for upskilling and reskilling the health and care workforce in digital and green skills. This initiative addresses public health needs, equipping professionals with the needed competencies to adapt to a rapidly changing health landscape.

title: Empowering Families: Advancing Breastfeeding through Collaboration, Innovation, and Health Literacy
creator: I Onyia, J Rosser, R Walsh
description: Issue/problemThe World Health Organisation (WHO) recommends that babies are exclusively fed breastmilk for the first 6 months of life. This gives babies the best start in life and offers health benefits to both the child and mother. Breastfed babies are less likely to have chest and gastrointestinal infections, develop asthma, eczema, and are less likely to become obese.

title: Health literacy as a determinant of healthcare access in refugees: a systematic review
creator: M Georgiadou, M Christodoulou-Devledian, A Heraclides, D Sakellariou
description: BackgroundRefugees and asylum seekers often face unique challenges in navigating healthcare systems, including potential gaps in health literacy. Health literacy - the ability to access, understand, appraise, and apply health information - is a critical determinant of healthcare access and health outcomes.

title: Caring for our informal caregivers: scoping review on loneliness interventions and their components
creator: V Knapen, A Ten Brug, R Willems, F E Witkamp, A Oenema
description: BackgroundInformal caregivers have an indispensable role in current society, yet they are at risk of experiencing loneliness. In order to protect and support sustainable caregiving, it is important to prevent or reduce loneliness among these groups. Currently, there is no overview of interventions aimed at informal caregiver loneliness and the components of those interventions.

title: How income, perception of scientists, and health literacy shape the use of non-conventional medicine
creator: M Duplaga
description: BackgroundThe use of non-conventional medicine (NCM) remains widespread, despite the lack of scientific evidence supporting its practices. This phenomenon raises public health concerns, particularly due to the risk of delayed access to appropriate treatment. The main aim of this study was to analyze the determinants of NCM services utilization.

title: The effect of ambient air pollutants on cardiac arrhythmia hospital admissions in Ireland
creator: K I Quintyne, C Kelly, P Kenny
description: AimExposure to poor ambient air quality and cardiovascular disease (CVD) has been investigated in numerous studies; whether ambient air pollutants are a cause of development of CVD, however, remains unclear. This study aimed to examine the relationship between COVID-19 transport restrictions and hospital admissions due to CVD specifically cardiac arrhythmias in Dublin city and county for 2020.

title: Impact of London’s Ultra Low Emission Zone on lung development in children: the CHILL cohort study
creator: H E Wood, H Hajmohammadi, R E Dove, J Scales, J Mitchell, A Sheikh, W J Gauderman, G Randhawa, I S Mudway, C J Griffiths
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundTraffic-related air pollution (TRAP) impairs children's lung development, increasing the risk of chronic lung disease and early mortality. To reduce TRAP, cities worldwide are introducing Clean Air Zones (CAZs), but evidence of their health impacts is limited. London's CAZ, targeting all petrol and diesel vehicles and called the Ultra Low Emission Zone (ULEZ), was implemented in 2019, providing a natural experiment to assess the health impacts of such pollution-mitigation strategies.

title: Building trust and fostering collaboration for equitable access to medicines in North Macedonia
creator: P Vracko, E Aragon de Leon
description: Under Phase IV of the UHC Partnership, North Macedonia focused on strengthening health system governance and health policy development, with key investments in institutional capacity, health workforce planning, primary health care (PHC), sustainable health financing, and access to medicines. Efforts included training Ministry of Health professionals in policy analysis, strategic planning, and evidence-based decision-making while enhancing coordination and policy coherence.

title: Psychiatric risk among concerned significant others of people with alcohol or drug use problems
creator: E Sundin
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundBeing a concerned significant other (CSO) to someone with alcohol or illicit drug use problems can cause stress and strain, increasing the risk of mental health issues. However, population studies on mental health in this group are rare. This study aimed to examine the association between exposure to harm from others’ substance use and psychiatric conditions up to two years later among adults in Sweden.

title: The Screen Effect: How Technology is Shaping Our Health
creator: J Riopel-Meunier, P Poirier, M E Piché
description: Leisure screen time is a key sedentary behavior that may influence various aspects of physical and mental health. This study examines the associations between screen time, meeting physical activity guidelines, self-reported health, and mental health in the Quebec population, considering sex differences. This study uses data from the 2017-2018 Canadian Community Health Survey, a cross-sectional and nationally representative survey.

title: 2.D. Round table: Responding to climate change impacts on mental health in Europe
creator: Organised by: European Climate and Health Observatory, Chair persons: Aleksandra Kazmierczak (Denmark), Andrea Schmidt (Austria)
description: Climate change impacts on mental health come in various forms. They include the trauma of experiencing extreme weather events and the longer-term effects thereof, such as PTSD or depression; implications of heat for persons with mental health conditions, in particular those on certain medications; as well as climate anxiety, i.e.

title: Finnish local health systems leaders’ approaches to change reflect resilience capacities
creator: S Karreinen, K Janhonen, L Kihlström, H Paananen, M Viita-aho, L K Tynkkynen
description: BackgroundOne key to public health preparedness is to understand how local level healthcare organisations build resilience. This qualitative study adds to the understanding of the role of leadership in this process by studying how local health system leaders’ approaches to change reflect health system resilience capacities. Furthermore, it explores what triggers and hinders organisational change during a crisis.

title: General perceptions of digitalisation and its impact on the use of digital health applications
creator: B Babitsch, N Hannemann
description: BackgroundDigitalisation shapes modern life and healthcare. Research has shown that digital health applications (DHA) are associated with better health outcomes, but have also revealed negative effects and increased inequalities. To date, little research has examined the role of general perceptions of digitalisation in DHA adoption and in relation to social determinants.

title: Impact of physical activity and diet in health-adjusted life expectancy: A PAF approach
creator: D Lee, S Oh
description: BackgroundAccording to WHO, physical inactivity and unhealthy diet are major risk factors for NCDs globally. GBD studies established causal relationships between these factors and major ncds cancer, heart disease, and diabetes. Despite known benefits, 90% of Korean adolescents and 45% of adults don't meet recommended physical activity levels, with fruit/vegetable consumption below WHO recommendations.

title: Plant-based diets in the Finnish adult population: findings from the Healthy Finland survey
creator: M Simojoki, N E Kaartinen, M Maukonen, L Paalanen, L Sares-Jäske, T Suikki, H Tapanainen, S Männistö
description: BackgroundPlant-based diets have the potential to benefit both human and planetary health. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence of plant-based diets (vegan, lacto-vegetarian, pescatarian, and semi-vegetarian) in the Finnish adult population.MethodsWe used data from the national Healthy Finland survey (2022-2023, n = 28,153, response rate 46%, aged 20 years or older).

title: Leaving no one behind in digital health: is Poland on the right track?
creator: M Duplaga
description: Since EU accession, Internet penetration in Poland has increased significantly and now reaches roughly 85 % of adults. Yet a digital divide persists: many seniors, rural dwellers, and low-income households remain offline or lack digital skills, hampering their access to modern public services, including healthcare. The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated digital health adoption.

title: School food interventions and their impact on child nutrition in Europe: a scoping review
creator: I Vidal, M Franco, P Domínguez, N Cohen, J Díez
description: BackgroundSchool food interventions help improve child nutrition. Evidence in Europe up to 2020 was scarce and inconclusive. This scoping review aimed to update and synthesize evidence on the impact of school food interventions on nutritional status among children and adolescents (0-19 years) in Europe, and to identify barriers, facilitators, and theoretical frameworks.MethodsWe followed PRISMA guidelines for this scoping review.

title: The role of public health professionals when crime are punishment dominate the debate
creator: A Sarkadi
description: Children under the age of 15 are recruited by criminal networks and commit serious crimes. There is now a consensus that gang crime is one of the biggest societal challenges facing Sweden. The political debate has had a clear focus on repressive measures.

title: Reflecting digital transformations in public health curricula: guidance for public health schools
creator: S Buttigieg, R Hrzic, BLH Wong, A Macedo Silva, KF Conyard, P Kostkova, M Codd, NM Schutte, R van Kessel
description: Public health education and training must include digital skills to maximise the positive public health impact of digital technologies. While these tools have proven valuable, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic, most public health curricula have not yet prioritised teaching digital skills and their implementation throughout essential public health functions.

title: Exploring national health literacy policy journeys
creator: A Schlacher, Y Arabska, B Brady, C Dietscher, C Le, A Ljubič, C Straßmayr, É Bíró
description: BackgroundThe WHO Action Network on Measuring Population and Organizational Health Literacy (M-POHL) aims to enhance health literacy (HL) in the WHO European Region by providing high-quality data on population and organizational health literacy and developing evidence-based recommendations to support political decisions.MethodsM-POHL's project on Evidence-based Policy and Practice (EVPOP) developed a policy guide structured around the Public Health Action Cycle.

title: Coevolution of education and income inequalities in mortality
creator: L Tarkiainen, O Östergren, L Dei Bardi, P Martikainen
description: BackgroundEducation and income are independent predictors of mortality, but they also interact so that educational inequalities in mortality are larger at low levels of income. However, the average educational attainment in high-income countries has risen during recent decades and it is unclear how the interplay between education and income on mortality has changed over time.

title: From Waste to Styrene–Butadiene (SBR) Reuse: Developing PP/SBR/SEP Mixtures with Carbon Nanotubes for Antistatic Application
creator: Edson Duarte de Melo Sobrinho, Eduardo da Silva Barbosa Ferreira, Flávio Urbano da Silva, Elieber Barros Bezerra, Renate Maria Ramos Wellen, Edcleide Maria Araújo, Carlos Bruno Barreto Luna, Markus Gahleitner
description: Styrene–butadiene rubber (SBR) waste from the shoe industry was repurposed to produce polypropylene (PP)-based compounds, with the aim of evaluating their antistatic potential. Styrene–ethylene–propylene (SEP) was added as a compatibilizing agent, while carbon nanotubes (MWCNT) were incorporated as a conductive nanofiller. The polymer compounds were processed in an internal mixer, and injection molded.

title: Association between suicide and access to mental health care in Portugal, 2019-2021
creator: I F Medeiros, A C Gomes, I Rodrigues, L Senna
description: BackgroundSuicide is a major public health issue in Portugal, where mental health disorders often go undertreated or even untreated. This study explores the association between access to mental health care and suicide rates in mainland Portugal from 2019 to 2021, aiming to understand how healthcare accessibility impacts suicide prevention efforts.

title: The Physiological Mechanism of Exogenous Melatonin on Improving Seed Germination and the Seedling Growth of Red Clover (Trifolium pretense L.) under Salt Stress
creator: Rui Liu, Ting Wang, Jiajie Wang, Di Yan, Yijia Lian, Zhengzong Lu, Yue Hong, Xue Yuan, Ye Wang, Runzhi Li
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Salt stress can affect various physiological processes in plants, ultimately hindering their growth and development. Melatonin (MT) can effectively resist multiple abiotic stresses, improving plant stress resistance. To analyze the mechanism of exogenous MT to enhance salt tolerance in red clover, we conducted a comprehensive study to examine the influence of exogenous MT on various parameters, including seed germination indices, seedling morphological traits, and physiological and photosynthetic indicators, using four distinct red clover varieties (H1, H2, H3, and H4).

title: Gender inequalities in caring roles – evidence on women’s material deprivation
creator: R-M Savela, J McKenzie
description: BackgroundEurope has faced multiple crises, including inflation, rising living and food costs, and COVID-19, worsening social inequalities. Economic hardships may impact the material deprivation of older adults, but little is known about how older adults with different caring roles may have been affected and whether there are other social determinants influencing their material deprivation and roles.

title: Distance and Coverage Geospatial Analysis of Routine vs Campaign Immunization in Sindh, Pakistan
creator: S Khalid, A Mahmood Abbasi, S Samrina, I Ali, C Moretti Anfossi, M Owais Siddiqui
description: BackgroundThe Zindagi Mehfooz Electronic Immunization Registry (ZM-EIR) has improved immunization coverage tracking in Sindh, Pakistan. However, to address missed vaccinations in underserved areas, the government launched the Big Catch-up campaign (BCU). Integrating ZM-EIR data with geospatial techniques allows for assessing and tracking immunization services in these areas.

title: Aminoethoxyvinylglicine and 1-Methylcyclopropene: Effects on Preharvest Drop, Fruit Maturity, Quality, and Associated Gene Expression of ‘Honeycrisp’ Apples in the US Mid-Atlantic
creator: Emily Johnson, Macarena Farcuh, Dongliang Qiu, Caihong Zhong
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Preharvest fruit drop is one of the main challenges in apple production as it can lead to extensive crop losses in commercially important cultivars including ‘Honeycrisp’. Plant growth regulators, such as aminoethoxyvinylglicine (AVG) and 1-methylcyclopropene (1-MCP), which hinder ethylene biosynthesis and perception, respectively, can control preharvest fruit drop, but an assessment of their effects in ‘Honeycrisp’ fruit grown under US mid-Atlantic conditions is lacking. In this study, we evaluated the effects of AVG (130 mg a.i. L−1) and 1-MCP (150 mg a.i.

title: Pesticide exposure profiles through tap water consumption in the NutriNet-Santé cohort in 2022
creator: E Meyer, J Berlivet, B Allès, M Touvier, D Lairon, L Gamet-Payrastre, H Guillou, R Vidal, E Kesse-Guyot, J Baudry
description: BackgroundPesticide residues in tap water from past and current agriculture are widespread, but health effects of exposure to individual pesticides and mixtures are understudied. This study identifies pesticide exposure profiles from tap water to support future research.MethodsIndividual pesticide exposure through tap water was estimated in a subsample (n = 17,833; mean age 62y (±11.

title: Socioeconomic deprivation and congenital anomalies: spatial patterns in Portugal, 2010–2021
creator: C Aniceto, P Braz, A Machado, C Matias-Dias
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundCongenital anomalies (CA) include structural/functional malformations, chromosomal anomalies, and other genetic diseases arising during intrauterine life. Although a link between socioeconomic inequalities and CA is suggested evidence in Portugal remains scarce. This study analyzed the geographic distribution of CA prevalence rate (PR) and the European Deprivation Index (EDI), and their spatial autocorrelation in mainland Portugal, using national CA registry data from 2010-2021.MethodsObservational ecological study using cases reported to the national CA registry (2010-2021).

title: Demographic and Epidemiological Transitions Across Africa: A Regional Policy Perspective
creator: F Ciccacci, F Basile, C Iazzolino, M Cicala, M Carestia, C Mosconi, C De Santo, P Germano, G Liotta, S Orlando
description: BackgroundAfrica is undergoing demographic and epidemiological transitions marked by population growth and a shift from communicable to non-communicable diseases (NCDs). These transitions vary by region and impact public health priorities. This study compares demographic and disease trends across five African regions to inform policy.MethodsWe conducted a descriptive study using secondary data.

title: Integrated Psycho-Socio-Educational Programmes for Women Victims of Gender-Based Violence
creator: María Cristina Lopes-Dos-Santos, Sagrario Anaut-Bravo, Victor R Prybutok, Walter R Schumm
description: Although women victims of gender-based violence suffer health and self-care issues, there is still a lack of coordinated integrated support programmes aimed at mitigating the socio-health impact of gender-based violence on women that are suitably adapted to new social contexts.

title: Association Between Visceral Fat Area and Glycated Hemoglobin in Type 2 Diabetics: A Retrospective Study
creator: Beibei Luo, Wenbo Xu, Lei Feng, Jingyi Chen, Rui Shi, Huiying Cao
description: IntroductionObesity is a risk factor for the development of type 2 diabetes (T2DM) as well as its associated metabolic complications. Central obesity, characterized by an increased visceral fat area (VFA), is contributed to the development of T2DM. However, the relationship between VFA and HbA1c is not particularly clear.

title: Efficient Solution-Phase Dipeptide Synthesis Using Titanium Tetrachloride and Microwave Heating
creator: Palmira Alessia Cavallaro, Marzia De Santo, Rocco Marinaro, Emilia Lucia Belsito, Angelo Liguori, Antonella Leggio, Oxana V Galzitskaya
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Microwaves have been successfully employed in the Lewis acid titanium tetrachloride-assisted synthesis of peptide systems. Dipeptide systems with their amino function differently protected with urethane protecting groups have been synthesized in short periods of time and with high yields. The formation of the peptide bond between the two reacting amino acids was achieved in pyridine by using titanium tetrachloride as a condensing agent and heating the reaction mixture with a microwave reactor.

title: Comparison of Post-Vaccination Response between mRNA and Vector Vaccines against SARS-CoV-2 in Terms of Humoral Response after Six Months of Observation
creator: Sebastian Slomka, Patrycja Zieba, Oskar Rosiak, Anna Piekarska
description: Background: The emergence of the SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) pandemic has accelerated work on the creation of effective vaccines, both in terms of previously known vector vaccines and new-generation (mRNA) vaccines. The scientific research on vaccination against COVID-19 infection is limited; therefore, understanding how the immune system responds to vaccines is critical.

title: GPU Implementation of the Improved CEEMDAN Algorithm for Fast and Efficient EEG Time–Frequency Analysis
creator: Zeyu Wang, Zoltan Juhasz
description: Time–frequency analysis of EEG data is a key step in exploring the internal activities of the human brain. Studying oscillations is an important part of the analysis, as they are thought to provide the underlying mechanism for communication between neural assemblies.

title: Multisensory System for Long-Term Activity Monitoring to Facilitate Aging-in-Place
creator: Sergio Lluva-Plaza, Ana Jiménez-Martín, David Gualda-Gómez, José Manuel Villadangos-Carrizo, Juan Jesús García-Domínguez
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Demographic changes and an ageing population require more effective methods to confront the increased prevalence of chronic diseases which generate dependence in older adults as well as an important rise in social expenditure. The challenge is not only to increase life expectancy, but also to ensure that the older adults can fully enjoy that moment in their lives, living where they wish to (private home, nursing home, …).

title: Parameter-Free State Estimation Based on Kalman Filter with Attention Learning for GPS Tracking in Autonomous Driving System
creator: Xue-Bo Jin, Wei Chen, Hui-Jun Ma, Jian-Lei Kong, Ting-Li Su, Yu-Ting Bai, Mohammad Aldibaja
description: GPS-based maneuvering target localization and tracking is a crucial aspect of autonomous driving and is widely used in navigation, transportation, autonomous vehicles, and other fields.The classical tracking approach employs a Kalman filter with precise system parameters to estimate the state.

title: The green transition and sustainability reporting in the Wellbeing Services County of Päijät-Häme
creator: R-M Hämäläinen, A Toivanen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The health and social services are responsible for approximately 6.5% of global greenhouse gas emissions in Finland. Without significant changes, these emissions will continue to rise. Therefore, service providers need to address their environmental footprint without compromising patient safety. Since the national reform in 2023, the Wellbeing Services County of Päijät-Häme has been responsible for providing health, social, and rescue services for the region of Päijät-Häme, which has a population of 200,000 people.

title: Glucose-Dependent Insulinotropic Polypeptide Inhibits AGE-Induced NADPH Oxidase-Derived Oxidative Stress Generation and Foam Cell Formation in Macrophages Partly via AMPK Activation †
creator: Michishige Terasaki, Hironori Yashima, Yusaku Mori, Tomomi Saito, Naoto Inoue, Takanori Matsui, Naoya Osaka, Tomoki Fujikawa, Makoto Ohara, Sho-ichi Yamagishi, Ida Daniela Perrotta
description: Glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) of the incretin group has been shown to exert pleiotropic actions. There is growing evidence that advanced glycation end products (AGEs), senescent macromolecules formed at an accelerated rate under chronic hyperglycemic conditions, play a role in the pathogenesis of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease in diabetes.

title: Gender differences in healthcare experience: evidence from Hong Kong hospital surveys (2010-2020)
creator: Y Tian, ELY Wong, H Qiu, H Wang, AWL Cheung, EK Yeoh
description: BackgroundUnderstanding potential gender disparities in patient experiences is critical for promoting health equity. In Hong Kong, where healthcare services are known for their accessibility and quality, it remains unclear whether males and females experience care differently.MethodsThis study conducted a secondary analysis of region-wide inpatient experience surveys collected between 2010 and 2020 in Hong Kong public hospitals.

title: Institutional Conflicts of Interest in Human Health Research – a Scoping Review
creator: A Haarmann, H Goodarzi, A Pachanov, C Kugler, E Akl, K Gooßen, D Pieper
description: BackgroundConflict of interests (CoIs) can influence decision making in health research, raising concerns about transparency and integrity. Institutional CoIs (iCoIs) can arise for individuals and institutions alike when holding any interest affects the research process or its outcome. While progress has been made in research on individual CoIs, iCoIs remain largely unexplored.

title: CO2 mission benefits of shifting car trips towards sustainable modes in Finnish city regions
creator: E Suomalainen, V Heikinheimo, A Rehunen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundShifting from car use to walking, cycling, or public transport increases physical activity and decreases transport-related CO2 emissions. The potential for sustainable travel remains, however, poorly understood.MethodsWe exploited Finland's National Travel Survey (NTS) 2021 (n = 8815 respondents in city regions, n = 562 in Helsinki) to estimate how many everyday trips chains by car could be replaced with sustainable modes, i.e.

title: Assessment of dementia knowledge, attitudes, and risk awareness among outpatients in Eskişehir
creator: S Sert, B Karagöz, D Arslantaş, A Ünsal
description: BackgroundDementia is a major public health issue due to its global prevalence, economic burden, and modifiable risk factors. Knowledge of dementia and its risk factors, along with individual attitudes, can influence access to care and quality of life. This study aimed to assess dementia-related knowledge, attitudes, and risk awareness among outpatients.

title: Subjective memory impairment and associated health factors in older adults
creator: B Gaertner, J Fuchs, R Kuhnert, H Neuhauser
description: BackgroundSubjective memory impairment (SMI) is predictive for dementia, cognitive decline and mortality. This nationwide population-based study examines the prevalence of SMI among older adults and its associations with demographics and age-related health indicators.MethodsGesundheit 65+ is a representative health survey of people aged 65 years and older in Germany (06/2021-04/2023). A total of 3,235 participants (44.6% women, mean age 78.

title: Is the EU on track for digital public health? A checklist for assessing the national preparedness
creator: L Maaß, B Li Han Wong, M M Kuhrn, S Buttigieg, R Hrzic, M Shokralla, H Lyshol, E Petelos, D Lingri, D Ivancovic
description: To ensure that European Union (EU) health-related regulations achieve their intended impact across member states, national systems must be equipped with robust technical infrastructure, coherent regulatory frameworks, and sustainable investment strategies. However, varying levels of digital readiness pose significant challenges to uniform implementation.

title: Acute Phase Reactants as Predictors of CKD Incidence in Africans: The RODAM Cohort Study
creator: M Mungamba, F Chilunga, E L van der Linden, E Beune, C F Hayfron-Benjamin, KAC Meeks, L Vogt, B J van den Born, B Nkeh-Chungag, C Agyemang
description: BackgroundChronic kidney disease (CKD) and chronic inflammation are highly prevalent in African populations, yet their relationship remains understudied. We examined the association between acute phase reactants (C-reactive protein and ferritin) as markers of acute and chronic inflammation and the incidence of CKD seven years later in a prospective Ghanaian population-based cohort.

title: Psychotropic use and psychotropic polypharmacy in intellectual disability - a national cohort study
creator: V Virtanen, L Saastamoinen, A Teittinen, H Vesala, S Miettinen, M Arvio, A M Tolppanen
description: IntroductionPsychotropic medication use and psychotropic polypharmacy are common in people with intellectual disabilities. However, representative, population-based studies on this topic are scarce. We evaluated the prevalence of psychotropic use and psychotropic polypharmacy in a Finnish nationwide cohort of people with intellectual disabilities.

title: Identifying population groups at risk of a very weak experience of social inclusion in Finland
creator: L Leemann, M Nousiainen, A Keto-Tokoi, A-M Isola
description: BackgroundThe experience of social inclusion (ESI) is an important part of psychosocial wellbeing and has significant public health implications. ESI includes aspects of agency, belonging, social support, meaningfulness, and trust, which may facilitate healthier behaviors. Previous studies also showed that ESI helps individuals to cope with difficult life situations, such as protecting adolescents from anxiety during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Exploring epidemic decision-making and the role of the public health institute in Germany
creator: A Berner-Rodoreda, C Franz, I Hunger, N Baum, K Bozorgmehr, J Hanefeld, T Bärnighausen
description: BackgroundThe nexus of politics and science played a crucial role during COVID-19. As pandemic measures are re-assessed, we explore evidence-informed decision-making in Germany during COVID-19 with a particular focus on Germany's National Public Health Institute (NPHI): What role did it play in the generation and coordination of evidence? To what extent and through which pathways did evidence inform political decisions?

title: Bridging mental health gaps: realist insights into community support for migrant informal carers
creator: MHL Hollaar, P L Kocken, O Uysal-Bozkir, P Buis, M Smedts, S Denktaş
description: BackgroundInformal carers with a migration background supporting a relative with a mental illness face barriers like stigma and cultural misunderstandings. The They Aren't Mental?! (TANM) intervention uses community-based peer education via ambassadors to reduce taboos, improve access to care, and enhance social support in informal carers.

title: Estimating health utility associated with mental well-being: mapping GHQ-12 responses onto EQ-5D-5L
creator: Z Mao, J Bilcke, K Pepermans, N Hens, P Beutels
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundMental well-being measures are common in population surveys but cannot be directly used for utility-based economic evaluations. Existing mapping studies, mostly pre-Covid-19, relied on linear regression, and may not reflect individuals’ evolving preferences on quality of life. This study explores methods to estimate health utility associated with mental well-being, by linking EQ-5D-5L and GHQ-12 responses collected in a large population sample.MethodsWe used data from 12701 respondents participating in the 46th Wave of the Belgian “Great Corona Study”, in March 2022.

title: 11.G. Skills building seminar: The Future is Core, Hackathon: Next-Gen Professionals Sustaining the ASPHER Core Curriculum Programme
creator: Organised by: ASPHER Core Curriculum Programme, Chair persons: Karl F Conyard (Ireland), Mary Codd (Ireland)
description: BackgroundThe ASPHER Core Curriculum for Public Health (CCP) is a landmark framework for shaping competent, responsive public health professionals. Yet, its continued relevance depends on the active engagement of those who will carry it forward - early career professionals (ECPs) in both public health academia and practice.

title: Improving Roma Women’s Health in Greece: A Comprehensive Health Promotion and Prevention Program
creator: P Karnaki, T Georgakopoulou, N Drougos, E Zioga, A Tsima, A Veloudaki
description: Roma people remain one of the most vulnerable groups in Europe and in Greece, as they continue to face difficult living conditions and discrimination in access to health, social protection, employment and adequate housing. The health of Roma women is highly vulnerable, with high rates of pregnancy and maternal complications, chronic conditions and mental health problems reported.

title: Psychosocial support for student loneliness: A pilot of Groups 4 Health at Helsinki University
creator: I Mankki, S Salakka, S Martikainen, H Kis, V Gergov, J Lahti
description: BackgroundLoneliness and psychological distress are common among Finnish university students, with rates higher than in the general population. These issues significantly impact mental health and well-being. Groups 4 Health (G4H) is a group-based intervention designed to improve social connectedness. While G4H has been shown to reduce loneliness in Australian students, its effectiveness in European university settings remains untested.

title: Pyrroloquinoline Quinone Alleviates Intestinal Inflammation and Cell Apoptosis via the MKK3/6-P38 Pathway in a Piglet Model
creator: Caiyun Huang, Xuanci Yu, Ziyuan Du, Zhihao Zhu, Chenyu Shi, Ang Li, Fenglai Wang
description: This study investigates the underlying mechanism through which dietary supplementation of pyrroloquinoline quinone disodium (PQQ) alleviates intestinal inflammation and cell apoptosis in piglets challenged with lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Seventy-two barrows were divided into three groups: control (CTRL), LPS challenged (LPS), and LPS challenged with PQQ supplementation (PQQ + LPS).

title: The role of socioeconomic factors in perinatal mortality: a case-control study in Istanbul
creator: S Girgin, S TuncNakis, O Karabacak, M A Sezerol, S Hidiroglu, P Ay
description: BackgroundSocioeconomic inequalities affect perinatal mortality (PM). This study aimed to investigate the relationship between socioeconomic status (SES) and PM in a district of Istanbul using a comprehensive SES index for the first time in Türkiye.MethodsThis case-control study was conducted in Istanbul, including perinatal deaths (2021-2023) as cases and randomly selected live births from the same period and district as controls.

title: The Impact of Thyroiditis on the Immune Profile in Young Patients with Uncomplicated Type 1 Diabetes
creator: Jolanta Neubauer-Geryk, Małgorzata Myśliwiec, Katarzyna Zorena, Leszek Bieniaszewski
description: Autoimmune thyroid disease (AIT) is the most frequently linked autoimmune condition to type 1 diabetes (T1D). The analysis of immune profiles could provide valuable insights into the study of these diseases. This knowledge could play a crucial role in understanding the relationship between immune profiles and microcirculation structures and functions.

title: Long-term consequences of adolescent social media use on mental health in young adulthood
creator: M Zetterqvist, G S Brunborg, J Raninen
description: BackgroundThere are growing concerns that social media may negatively impact adolescents’ mental health. However, most studies are cross-sectional, or short-term longitudinal studies, limiting conclusions about long-term effects. This study investigates whether social media use at age 15/16 is associated with symptoms of depression and anxiety five years later. It also explores differences by gender, socioeconomic status (SES), and physical activity.

title: Characterization of Oxacillin-Resistant and Oxacillin-Susceptible mecA-Positive Staphylococcus pseudintermedius from Skin Lesions and Nasal Cavities of Dogs with Clinical Pyoderma
creator: Putu Ayu Sisyawati Putriningsih, Jaruwan Kampa, Suphattra Jittimanee, Patchara Phuektes
description: Simple SummaryStaphylococcus pseudintermedius is a common bacterium that causes skin infections in dogs and can occasionally infect humans, posing a public health risk. The presence of the mecA gene in this bacterium can lead to resistance against methicillin (oxacillin) and other beta-lactam antibiotics, which limits treatment options. This study investigated the characteristics of oxacillin-resistant and oxacillin-susceptible mecA-positive S.

title: High-Quality Single Crystalline Sc0.37Al0.63N Thin Films Enabled by Precise Tuning of III/N Atomic Flux Ratio during Molecular Beam Epitaxy
creator: Yuhao Yin, Rong Liu, Haiyang Zhao, Shizhao Fan, Jianming Zhang, Shun Li, Qian Sun, Hui Yang, Uwe Burghaus
description: We attained wurtzite ScxAl1−xN (0.16 ≤ x ≤ 0.37) thin films by varying the Sc and Al fluxes at a fixed active nitrogen flux during plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy. Atomic fluxes of Sc and Al sources via measured Sc percentage in as-grown ScxAl1−xN thin films were derived as the feedback for precise determination of the ScxAl1−xN growth diagram.

title: 8.G. Round table: Health and care workforce migration: how to navigate ethically and align global and European needs?
creator: Organised by: EUPHA Health and Care Workforce section, EUPHA Ethics in Public Health section, Faculty of Public Health UK and Global Network for Academic Public Health, WHO-CC Health Policy and Planning, WHO/Europe, Chair persons: Ellen Kuhlmann (EUPHA-HCW)
description: BackgroundHealth and care workforce (HCWF) migration increased globally and the HCWF crisis in high-income countries, armed conflicts and COVID-19 politics added new dynamics. These developments exacerbate inequalities between sending and receiving countries, challenging international regulations and calling for a critical reassessment of the Global Code and the promises of bilateral agreements and circular migration.

title: The efficacy of buprenorphine compared with dexmedetomidine in spinal anesthesia: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Joao Marcos Cansian, Angelo Zanin D'Angelo Giampaoli, Liege Caroline Immich, André Prato Schmidt, Andrei Sanson Dias
description: BackgroundThis study compares dexmedetomidine and buprenorphine as potential adjuvants for spinal anesthesia. Dexmedetomidine enhances sensory block and minimizes the need for pain medication, while buprenorphine, a long-acting opioid, exhibits a favorable safety profile compared to traditional opioids.MethodsPubMed, Cochrane and EMBASE were systematically searched in December 2023.

title: Wastewater epidemiology of respiratory viruses: implementation of a regional surveillance system
creator: L Viviani, R Vecchio, S Villa, A Fiorentino, E Ammoni, D Cereda, A Odone
description: Wastewater surveillance is an innovative epidemiological tool that detects pathogens in sewage, providing population-wide indicators of infectious disease circulation. It offers a cost-effective approach to gathering epidemiological data from large populations, including asymptomatic individuals. In Lombardy (Italy), the Regional Government activated a surveillance system based on wastewater analysis for three respiratory viruses: SARS-CoV-2, Influenza virus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV).

title: Behavioral risks and quality of life of Ukrainian refugees versus the Estonian general population
creator: G Opikova, R Rainer, J Saavaste, T Lai, J Haagsma
description: BackgroundRefugees constitute a vulnerable group that often experiences a lower health-related quality of life (HRQoL) than the general population. This study examines the association between HRQoL and behavioral risk profiles among Ukrainian female refugees and females from the Estonian general population.

title: Training potential of a teleoperated humanoid robot for use by a young psychiatrist during childcare leave
creator: Hiroko Kawahara, Nobukazu Kanchi, Megumi Kawata, Yuichiro Yoshikawa, Jun Baba, Taro Muramatsu, Hiroshi Ishiguro, Hirokazu Kumazaki
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundChildcare leave extensions can sometimes negatively affect the professional clinical training of early‐career psychiatrists in Japan. During childcare leave, being able to learn in the examination room while staying at home would be useful. Therefore, we developed a training system using a teleoperated robot (Sota) for young psychiatrists who wanted to participate in the examination room during childcare leave while remaining at home.Case PresentationWe report the case of a patient with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) comorbid with Tourette's disorders (P).

title: Women’s previous economic activity and later cognitive functioning. Findings from the Tromsø study
creator: B Halse, M Veenstra, B Strand
description: BackgroundThe aim was to investigate if persons’ economic histories in adulthood are associated with later cognitive function. Analyses exploited detailed income registers in Norway, dating back to 1967. At this time, it was arguably more common for adult women to be less economically active, enabling a sample of women with precisely measured variation in past economic activities.

title: Turn over the new leaf of the treatment in peptic ulcer bleeding: a review of the literature
creator: Meng-Hsuan Lu, Hsueh-Chien Chiang
description: Peptic ulcer bleeding is the most common cause of upper gastrointestinal bleeding, which has a high mortality risk. The standard therapy for acute peptic ulcer bleeding combines medication administration and endoscopic therapies. Both pharmacologic and endoscopic therapies have developed continuously in the past few decades.

title: Perspectives of key stakeholders on taxation of sugar-sweetened beverages in Slovenia
creator: A Brlek, O Stanojević Jerković, S Matak, M Gabrijelčič
description: BackgroundFree sugars are considered to be one of the most problematic nutrients in the daily diet, especially when we consume them through the intake of sugar-sweetened beverages (SSBs). Effectively designed tax on SSBs is often highlighted as one of the most successful measures to limit the intake of free sugars.

title: Rapid Impregnating Resins for Fiber-Reinforced Composites Used in the Automobile Industry
creator: Mei-Xian Li, Hui-Lin Mo, Sung-Kwon Lee, Yu Ren, Wei Zhang, Sung-Woong Choi
description: As environmental regulations become stricter, weight- and cost-effective fiber-reinforced polymer composites are being considered as alternative materials in the automobile industry. Rapidly impregnating resin into the reinforcing fibers is critical during liquid composite molding, and the optimization of resin impregnation is related to the cycle time and quality of the products.

title: Landscape structure and site characteristics influence whether the northern house martin Delichon urbicum occupies artificial nests
creator: Gianna Allera, Ramona Julia Heim, Aline Förster, Wieland Heim
description: Artificial nest sites can support populations of endangered species when they are correctly installed. Here we analysed the characteristics and conditions that determined whether the northern house martin Delichon urbicum occupied more than 300 artificial nests around the city of Münster, Germany. We found that artificial nest occupation rates were influenced by various environmental and temporal factors.

title: Avoiding road traffic injuries: 25 years of providing evidence on road safety at the city level
creator: K Pérez, E Santamariña-Rubio, M J López, L Artazcoz, J Ferrando, C Pastor, A A Hyder, C Borrell
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Description of the problemBarcelona, a dense Mediterranean city with high mobility and many motorcyclists, established a road traffic injury surveillance system in the early 1990s, integrating police, hospital, and forensic data. From 2000 to 2023, ten interventions were evaluated, including legislative measures (helmet law, motorcycle license, penalty point system) and infrastructure changes (speed cameras, 30 km/h zones, safe school routes, advanced stop lines for motorcycles, red-light cameras). Most evaluations used quasi-experimental designs with comparison groups.

title: Molecular Insights to the Structure-Interaction Relationships of Human Proton-Coupled Oligopeptide Transporters (PepTs)
creator: Yining Luo, Jingchun Gao, Xukai Jiang, Ling Zhu, Qi Tony Zhou, Michael Murray, Jian Li, Fanfan Zhou
description: Human proton-coupled oligopeptide transporters (PepTs) are important membrane influx transporters that facilitate the cellular uptake of many drugs including ACE inhibitors and antibiotics. PepTs mediate the absorption of di- and tri-peptides from dietary proteins or gastrointestinal secretions, facilitate the reabsorption of peptide-bound amino acids in the kidney, and regulate neuropeptide homeostasis in extracellular fluids.

title: Training health workers and community influencers to be Vaccine Champions: a mixed-methods RE-AIM evaluation
creator: Jessica Kaufman, Isabella Overmars, James Fong, Jemesa Tudravu, Rachel Devi, Litiana Volavola, Luisa Vodonaivalu, Kylie Jenkins, Julie Leask, Holly Seale, Yasmin Mohamed, Kshitij Joshi, Halitesh Datt, Sonya Sagan, Michelle Dynes, Monsurul Hoq, Margie Danchin
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionIncreasing trust and confidence in vaccines is a global priority, as countries have grappled with delivering COVID-19 vaccines, maintaining routine childhood vaccination rates and introducing new vaccines. Community-based vaccine promotion interventions are commonly implemented, but effectiveness evidence is limited.

title: Climate change threatens culturally and regionally relevant physical activities
creator: L Grout, C Pirkle, S Schmid, E Yokooji, T Sentell
description: BackgroundCulturally or regionally relevant physical activities (CRRPAs), such as traditional sports and games, deliver health benefits to individuals and communities. However, climate change may reduce participation in physical activities, especially those that are ice/snow-based (eg, Nordic skating, Kumoterki races, bandy).

title: Computational Amendment of Parenteral In Situ Forming Particulates’ Characteristics: Design of Experiment and PBPK Physiological Modeling
creator: Nada M El Hoffy, Ahmed S Yacoub, Amira M Ghoneim, Magdy Ibrahim, Hussein O Ammar, Nermin Eissa, Gábor Vasvári, Ádám Haimhoffer
description: Lipid and/or polymer-based drug conjugates can potentially minimize side effects by increasing drug accumulation at target sites and thus augment patient compliance. Formulation factors can present a potent influence on the characteristics of the obtained systems. The selection of an appropriate solvent with satisfactory rheological properties, miscibility, and biocompatibility is essential to optimize drug release.

title: Management of postintubation tracheal stenosis with bronchoscope methods—An experience from two centers
creator: Arvindran Alaga, Vineet Simhan, Srivatsa Lokeshwaran, Sunil Kumar K, Sanjana Chetana Shanmukhappa
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Tracheal stenosis is a common complication of endotracheal intubation or tracheostomy, resulting in significant morbidity and mortality. Bronchoscope interventions have been proposed as a safe alternative for the management of post‐intubation post‐intubation tracheal stenosis (PITS). Data for patients diagnosed with PITS across two hospitals, between 2021 and 2022, encompassing demographic, clinical, and procedural details were gathered from electronic medical records, and analysed.

title: Impact of childhood health adversities on late-life depression and mental health
creator: S Lee
description: BackgroundDrawing upon life course frameworks, the study examined the association between childhood health adversities and the psychological and mental well-being of older adults.MethodsThe study used data derived from the Survey of Health, Aging and Retirement in Europe (SHARE), Waves 5 (2013) 6 (2015) and 7 (2017). The baseline sample comprised 47,862 older adults aged 60 and above (mean age 71.

title: Development and Evaluation of Zinc and Iron Nanoparticles Functionalized with Plant Growth-Promoting Rhizobacteria (PGPR) and Microalgae for Their Application as Bio-Nanofertilizers
creator: Carlos Esteban Guardiola-Márquez, Edgar R. López-Mena, M. Eugenia Segura-Jiménez, Isaac Gutierrez-Marmolejo, Manuel A. Flores-Matzumiya, Shirley Mora-Godínez, Carmen Hernández-Brenes, Daniel A. Jacobo-Velázquez
description: Micronutrient deficiencies are widespread and growing global concerns. Nanoscale nutrients present higher absorption rates and improved nutrient availability and nutrient use efficiency. Co-application of nanofertilizers (NFs) with biological agents or organic compounds increases NF biocompatibility, stability, and efficacy. This study aimed to develop and evaluate zinc and iron bio-nanofertilizers formulated with plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) and microalgae.

title: Inhibitory Activity of Natural cis-Khellactone on Soluble Epoxide Hydrolase and Proinflammatory Cytokine Production in Lipopolysaccharides-Stimulated RAW264.7 Cells
creator: Jang Hoon Kim, Ji Hyeon Park, Sung Cheol Koo, Yun-Chan Huh, Mok Hur, Woo Tae Park, Youn-Ho Moon, Tae Il Kim, Byoung Ok Cho, Jinping Si, Shunxing Guo, Yongping Cai, Zhenming Yu
description: The pursuit of anti-inflammatory agents has led to intensive research on the inhibition of soluble epoxide hydrolase (sEH) and cytokine production using medicinal plants. In this study, we evaluated the efficacy of cis-khellactone, a compound isolated for the first time from the roots of Peucedanum japonicum.

title: Five Forms of Coerced “Self-Produced” Child Sexual Exploitation Material: A Critical Interpretive Synthesis
creator: Genevieve Bloxsom, Gemma McKibbin, Cathy Humphreys, Jennifer Davidson, Nick Halfpenny
description: This review explored how the phenomenon of coerced “self-produced” child sexual exploitation material (CSEM) has been constructed in the literature using Critical Interpretative Synthesis. Selected keywords were systematically searched on relevant databases. Types of papers included were: peer-reviewed research articles; conceptual papers; commentary papers; theses; book chapters; systematic reviews; and government reports.

title: Is public health losing its reach? The precautionary principle and European Union chemicals policy
creator: C Stephenson, M Koivusalo, A McCallum, S Atkins
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe precautionary principle is a regulatory tool that enables decision makers to protect the health of future generations in the face of scientific uncertainty by allowing for regulatory action before proof of harm is established. Where an action may pose serious or irreversible risks to human, animal, plant or environmental health in the European Region, proof that it is not harmful usually lies with the proposer, often industry.

title: About Research - Qualitative Data Collection: Photo Elicitation
creator: Sara L Gill
description: Photo elicitation is a qualitative data collection technique in which the researcher includes photographs or other visual images as part of participant interviews. The researcher might provide the photographs or might ask the participants to bring photographs to the interview. This technique enhances the breadth and depth of verbal qualitative interviews.

title: Ecogeography of Dioscorea remotiflora Kunth: An Endemic Species from Mexico
creator: Jocelyn Maira Velázquez-Hernández, José Ariel Ruíz-Corral, Noé Durán-Puga, Miguel Ángel Macías, Diego Raymundo González-Eguiarte, Fernando Santacruz-Ruvalcaba, Giovanni Emmanuel García-Romero, Agustín Gallegos-Rodríguez
description: Dioscorea remotiflora, a perennial climbing herbaceous plant native to Mexico, produces tubers with great nutritional and ethnobotanical value. However, most ecological aspects of this plant remain unknown, which limits its cultivation and use. This is why the objective of this research was to characterize the ecogeography of D.

title: Pentadecapeptide BPC 157 as Therapy for Inferior Caval Vein Embolization: Recovery of Sodium Laurate-Post-Embolization Syndrome in Rats
creator: Ivan Maria Smoday, Ivan Krezic, Luka Kalogjera, Vlasta Vukovic, Helena Zizek, Marija Skoro, Katarina Kasnik Kovac, Hrvoje Vranes, Ivan Barisic, Suncana Sikiric, Sanja Strbe, Marijan Tepes, Katarina Oroz, Slavica Zubcic, Mirjana Stupnisek, Lidija Beketic Oreskovic, Ivana Kavelj, Luka Novosel, Matea P
description: After inferior caval vein embolization therapy, post-embolization syndrome (sodium laurate 10 mg/kg, 0.1 mL into rat inferior caval vein, assessment at 15, 30, 60 min, prime lung lesions, thromboemboli occluding lung vessels), as a severe occlusion/occlusion-like syndrome, might be resolved as a whole by stable gastric pentadecapeptide BPC 157 therapy.

title: A phase II study of weekly carboplatin and concurrent radiotherapy in older adults with locally advanced non‐small cell lung cancer (LOGIK1902)
creator: Taishi Harada, Tomonari Sasaki, Hidenobu Ishii, Shinnosuke Takemoto, Yasushi Hisamatsu, Haruhiro Saito, Yasuto Yoneshima, Kazutoshi Komiya, Kosuke Kashiwabara, Katsuhiko Naoki, Tomohiro Ogawa, Hiroaki Takeoka, Koichi Saruwatari, Kensaku Ito, Yuko Tsuchiya‐Kawano, Keiko Mizuno, Takayuki Shimose, Yosh
description: BackgroundConcurrent chemoradiotherapy is the standard therapy for locally advanced non‐small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, there is little evidence supporting its use in older adults. Low‐dose daily carboplatin combined with thoracic radiotherapy is considered a standard regimen for this population.

title: Influence of Extrudate-Based Textural Properties on Pellet Molding Quality
creator: Wenxiu Tian, Xue Li, Wenjie Li, Aile Xue, Minyue Zheng, Xiao Lin, Yanlong Hong, Pradeep Kumar Bolla, Arun Butreddy
description: As the precursor of pellets, the extrudate has a direct impact on the molding quality of the pellets. Therefore, the correlation between the surface roughness of the extrudates and the molding quality of pellets with pure microcrystalline cellulose (MCC) formulations and those containing traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formulations was explored.

title: Radiofrequency Catheter Ablation in Patients with Supraventricular Tachycardia: A Cohort Study on Efficacy, Safety, Anxiety, and Quality of Life Outcomes
creator: Mohammad Taghi Hedayati Goudarzi, Mahsa Akbarian, Iman Bhia, Mehrdad Saravi, Hossein Soltaninejad
description: Background: Over the past two decades, radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA) has emerged as a leading treatment for cardiac arrhythmias due to its high efficacy, despite potential complications. This study evaluated success rates, complications, and the procedure’s impact on quality of life (QoL) and anxiety in patients with supraventricular arrhythmia (SVT).

title: The Role of Intraoperative Neurophysiological Monitoring in Intracranial Cavernous Malformation Surgery: A Narrative Review
creator: Mei Shao, Qi-Yang Huai, Jian-Wei Song, Fu-Qiang Wang, Yan-Na Li, Xia Li, Feng-Ling Wang
description: Cavernous malformations, also known as cavernous hemangiomas or cavernomas, are abnormal vascular lesions that can occur in various parts of the body, including intracranially. Surgical resection is often the preferred treatment for symptomatic or high-risk lesions located in eloquent or critical brain or spinal cord regions.

title: Population genetic structure and demographic of Spodoptera eridania (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae), an emerging soybean pest in Brazil
creator: Renato J Horikoshi, Frederico Nanini, Davi de S Fernandes, Geraldo U Berger, Patrick M Dourado, Ramiro F L Ovejero, Alberto S Corrêa
description: Spodoptera eridania (Stoll) is a key pest of soybean crops in Brazil. However, information about the physiology, behavior, and ecology of S. eridania, including its genetic variability within the agricultural landscape, remains scarce. In this study, we conducted an exploratory analysis of the genetic diversity, population structure, and demographic patterns of S. eridania in Brazil.

title: Integrating Novel Biomarkers into Clinical Practice: A Practical Framework for Diagnosis and Management of Cardiorenal Syndrome
creator: Georgios Aletras, Maria Bachlitzanaki, Maria Stratinaki, Emmanuel Lamprogiannakis, Ioannis Petrakis, Emmanuel Foukarakis, Yannis Pantazis, Michael Hamilos, Kostas Stylianou
description: Cardiorenal syndrome (CRS) reflects the intricate and bidirectional interplay between cardiac and renal dysfunction, commonly resulting in diagnostic uncertainty, therapeutic dilemmas and poor outcomes. While traditional biomarkers like serum creatinine (Cr) and natriuretic peptides remain widely used, their limitations in specificity, timing and contextual interpretation often hinder optimal management.

title: Detection of Tick-Borne Microorganisms, Anaplasmataceae and Piroplasmida, in Sorex spp. in Hokkaido, Japan
creator: Aya Zamoto-Niikura, Shigeharu Terui, Mizuki Sasaki, Minoru Nakao, Masakatsu Taira, Ken-Ichi Hanaki, Inaki Tirados
description: The habitats of shrews substantially overlap with those of rodents, which are well known as reservoirs for many tick-borne diseases. However, the ecological role of shrews (Mammalia: Eulipotyphla: Soricidae) remains poorly understood. We examined 103 Sorex spp. (S. unguiculatus, S. gracillimus, S. caecutiens) from Kushiro, Hokkaido, Japan, to investigate their relationships with ticks and tick-borne microorganisms, including Piroplasmida and Anaplasmataceae.

title: The Effect of the Nasal Airflow Reducer on Parasympathetic Activity in Adults: A Pilot and Exploratory Study
creator: Yen-Chang Lin, Jui-Kun Chiang, Hsueh-Hsin Kao, Tzu-Hao Lin, Tzu-Ying Hung, Yee-Hsin Kao
description: Background and Objectives: Boosting parasympathetic activity may enhance both physical and mental functions. In this study, we introduced the Lin Nasal Airflow Reducer (L.NAR), a silicone device designed to reduce nasal airflow. This pilot and exploratory study aimed to investigate the effect of L.NAR on parasympathetic activity in adults.

title: Biomechanical Effects of Cement Augmentation and Prophylactic Vertebroplasty on Adjacent Segment Stability in Multilevel Spinal Fusion: A Finite Element Analysis
creator: Jae Won Shin, Dae Hyeon Kim, Ki Mun Kang, Tae Hyun Park, Yu Rim Oh, Sung Jae Lee, Byung Ho Lee
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: Multilevel posterior spinal fusion to T10 often encounters complications such as screw loosening and proximal junctional kyphosis. Cement augmentation or prophylactic vertebroplasty is used to prevent these, but their biomechanical effects remain unclear. Methods: A validated finite element model (T8–pelvis) from CT data of a 57-year-old male was tested in five configurations: fusion only, fusion with cement augmentation at T10, T10–T11, T10–T11 plus T9 vertebroplasty, and T10–T11 plus T8–T9 vertebroplasty.

title: Patterns and Determinants of Dietary Supplement Use and Their Public Health Implications Among Adults in Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study
creator: Maha Al Turki, Fatmah Othman, Doaa Aljasser, Abeer Salman Alzaben
description: The consumption of dietary supplements is increasing worldwide, yet national data from Saudi Arabia remain limited. This study examined the prevalence, patterns, and predictors of dietary supplement use, with emphasis on vitamin intake. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 477 adults meeting inclusion criteria.

title: The Habitat Fragmentation and Suitability Evaluation of Mrs Hume’s Pheasant Syrmaticus humiae in Northwestern Guangxi, China
creator: Baodong Yuan, Ying Li, Zhicheng Yao
description: Simple SummaryThe Jinzhongshan region covers 38,716.6 hm2, including 1708 patches and 11 landscape types. Although the area of farmland and village only occupies 10%, their number and density have led Jinzhongshan habitats to fragment. The degree of connection of suitable habitat was found to be relatively low, and seven landscape indices were below 0.

title: Integrated Multi-Omics Reveal the Genetic and Metabolic Blueprint for Corn Straw Degradation in the White-Rot Fungus Irpex lacteus J2
creator: Jian Pang, Shizhen Zhao, Tao Hua, Jiahui Fan, Zhe Yan, Mingyuan Chen, Fan Zhao, Jingshi Yu, Qiaoxia Shang, Saheed Sabiu
description: Simple SummaryAgricultural waste, like corn straw, is an abundant resource that could be converted into valuable products such as biofuels, but its tough structure makes this challenging. A powerful wood-decaying fungus, Irpex lacteus J2, can efficiently break down this material, but the exact molecular processes it uses have been a mystery.

title: Reassessing Whether Biodegradable Microplastics Are Environmentally Friendly: Differences in Earthworm Physiological Responses and Soil Carbon Function Impacts
creator: Yuze Li, Dongxing Zhou, Hongyan Wang, Wenfei Zhu, Rui Wang, Yucui Ning
description: Biodegradable plastics are not a primary solution to plastic pollution, and empirical evidence on whether they are environmentally friendly remains lacking. In this study, we systematically compared the toxic effects of traditional microplastics (polypropylene, PP; polystyrene, PS) with biodegradable microplastics (polylactic acid, PLA; polyhydroxyalkanoates, PHA) on the haplic phaeozem ecosystem.

title: Comparative Outcomes of Day 3 and Day 5 Frozen–Thawed Embryo Transfers: A Retrospective Clinical Study
creator: Fatma Kılıç Hamzaoğlu, Serdar Dilbaz, Runa Özelçi, Onur Kaya, Emine Utlu Özen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Aim: This study aimed to compare the clinical pregnancy outcomes of Day 3 (cleavage-stage) and Day 5 (blastocyst) frozen–thawed embryo transfers in assisted reproductive technology (ART) cycles. Methods: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 6455 patients who underwent frozen–thawed embryo transfer (FET) between 1 April 2010 and 1 April 2023, at SBÜ Etlik Zübeyde Hanım Women’s Health Training and Research Hospital. Patients were categorized based on embryo transfer type, and clinical outcomes were compared using statistical analyses.

title: From Thinking to Creativity: The Interplay of Mathematical Thinking Perceptions, Mathematical Communication Dispositions, and Creative Thinking Dispositions
creator: Murat Genç, Mustafa Akıncı, İlhan Karataş, Özgür Murat Çolakoğlu, Nurbanu Yılmaz Tığlı
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Fostering mathematical thinking, communication, and creativity has become a central goal in mathematics education as these competencies are strongly linked to flexible problem solving and innovative engagement. Prior research has shown that students’ beliefs and dispositions play a crucial role in shaping their learning, strategy use, and persistence, yet limited evidence exists on how these constructs interrelate among pre-service elementary mathematics teachers. Addressing this gap, the present study examines the relationships among mathematical thinking perceptions, mathematical communication dispositions, and creative thinking dispositions.

title: Blue spaces and incident dementia: Differences by geospatial and historical contexts
creator: Kyle D. Moored, Michael R. Desjardins, Andrea L. Rosso, Gina S. Lovasi, Timothy M. Shields, Frank C. Curriero, Oscar L. Lopez, Michelle C. Carlson
